title: 2011 Pymble Legal Studies Trial
notes: Scanned paper read from rendered pages. No answer key is included. Question 17 has a wording error (“charges” for “charged”).

groups.stimulus: In the course of holding up a bottle shop and stealing the money from the cash register, John deliberately fired bullets into all the fridges, breaking many of the bottles.

questions.stem: Julio is on trial for murder. With whom does the burden of proof lie?
questions.answerNote: Crown bears the burden of proof.

questions.stem: John is cleaning his rifle when it discharges. A bullet from the gun hits Paul and kills him. Which element of criminal liability is lacking in this case?
questions.answerNote: Accidental discharge lacks mens rea (intent/recklessness); 'accident' is not an element.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of situational crime prevention?
questions.answerNote: Police patrols increase surveillance/risk to the offender; Situational prevention changes the environment. Others are deterrence or social prevention.

questions.stem: Which of the following are rights of an accused person in NSW?

options.B: Right to silence and right to a lawyer
options.C: Right to silence and right to a phone call
options.D: Security of person and right to a lawyer

questions.answerNote: Right to silence and right to a lawyer (LEPRA).

questions.stem: Which of the following mechanisms best protects an Australian citizen’s human rights?
questions.answerNote: Australia has no federal Bill of Rights, so D is not an existing mechanism; Common and statute law provide most real protection (Constitution has few express rights, treaties not directly enforceable). Plausible alternative: D, if the setter meant a Bill of Rights as the strongest mechanism in theory; Or C.

questions.stem: The term universal suffrage refers to which of the following rights?

options.C: To remain silent when questioned by the police
options.D: To vote freely for one’s elected representatives

questions.answerNote: Universal suffrage is the right of all adults to vote.

questions.stem: The United Nations has criticised the country of Nazalia over its human rights. Which of the following allows Nazalia to ignore the UN?
questions.answerNote: State sovereignty lets a nation reject external interference.

questions.stem: The police in Cooperville attempt to address high juvenile crime rates through establishing a Community Youth Centre to operate out of school hours. This is an example of which of the following?

options.A: Making crime more difficult to commit

questions.answerNote: Youth centre is a social/community crime prevention measure.

questions.stem: Fred is charged with sexual assault. What is the standard of proof in this case?

options.B: On the doctrine of natural justice

questions.answerNote: Criminal standard is beyond reasonable doubt.

questions.stem: Which of the following could be considered preliminary crimes?
questions.answerNote: Conspiracy and attempt are preliminary (inchoate) crimes. B includes treason (not preliminary) and A, D are not.

questions.stem: What is the main role of the police in New South Wales?

options.B: Send people who are guilty of crimes to prison
options.C: Ensure victims of crime receive justice
options.D: Enforce the criminal laws of the state

questions.answerNote: Police enforce the criminal law.

questions.stem: The offence John has committed can be described using which of the following terms?

options.C: Summary and offence against the person
options.D: Indictable and offence against the person

questions.answerNote: Armed robbery is indictable and generally classed as an offence against the person (violence/threat). Plausible alternative: B if robbery is classed as economic/property.

questions.stem: During sentencing, the judge would consider the breaking of the bottles to be which of the following?
questions.answerNote: Damage beyond what was needed is an aggravating factor in sentencing.

questions.stem: Which of the following penalties is John most likely to receive?
questions.answerNote: Armed robbery with firearm discharged attracts imprisonment.

questions.stem: Which of the following rights are included in the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights?
questions.answerNote: ICCPR protects liberty (art 9).

questions.stem: The idea that a child under 10 is considered incapable of committing a crime is contained in which of the following principles?
questions.answerNote: Doli incapax.

questions.stem: Danny has been charges with shoplifting. He is 17. In which court will the matter be heard?
questions.answerNote: 17-year-old is a child (under 18), so Children's Court.

questions.stem: Which of the following organisations would undertake a trial about genocide?
questions.answerNote: ICC tries genocide.

questions.stem: What human rights are identified as express rights in the Australian Constitution?

options.B: Freedom of religion and sexual preference
options.C: Freedom of religion and right of assembly
options.D: Freedom of religion and trial by jury

questions.answerNote: Express rights: s116 religion, s80 jury trial for indictable federal offences.

questions.stem: Which of the following courts does not have appellate criminal jurisdiction?
questions.answerNote: Local Court has no criminal appellate jurisdiction (appeals from Local Court go to District Court).
